title: Onshore oil and gas production flow
lead: Oil and gas start at a drilled well (1). Reservoir fluid is lifted to the surface by an electric submersible pump (2) or a pumpjack (3) and flows through flowlines to the manifold (4) at the gathering station. There the separator (5) splits gas, oil and water; the gas boot (6) releases leftover gas from the oil before it enters the wash tank (7), which cleans the remaining water out of the oil; clean oil is stored and sent through the export pipeline (8). Gas is compressed or burned at the flare (9), while produced water is injected back into the reservoir (10). All pumps, motors and compressors run on electricity from the power pole (11) and transformer (12).

ui.steps: How it works, step by step

alt: Onshore oil and gas production flow from the well to the gathering station, with the electrical system: drilling rig, ESP well and pumpjack well, manifold, separator, gas boot, wash tank, storage tank and shipping pump, compressor and flare, water injection pump, power pole, and transformer. Pick a number to read the explanation.

stages.name: Drilling Rig
stages.fn: Drills the well bore down into the reservoir, then sets casing and cement so the hole stays stable and the rock layers are isolated.
stages.story: Everything starts at the well. The rig drills a hole from the surface down into the oil-bearing reservoir. The bit is turned through the drill string while drilling mud is pumped continuously to cool the bit, carry cuttings up and hold back formation pressure. Every few hundred metres the hole is lined with steel pipe (casing) and cemented, so the wall does not collapse and the rock layers do not leak into each other.
steps: The drawworks raise and lower the traveling block; the top drive turns the drill string and the bit at the bottom of the hole.
Mud pumps push mud through the standpipe and hose, down inside the drill pipe and out of the bit nozzles.
The mud returns up the space between the pipe and the hole wall (the annulus), carrying cuttings to the surface.
At the surface a shale shaker screens out the cuttings; clean mud returns to the mud tank and is pumped again (closed circulation).
At a set depth the casing is run and cement is pumped into the space between casing and rock; after it sets, drilling continues with a smaller bit.
A BOP is installed on the wellhead: if formation pressure suddenly rises (a kick), the BOP is closed to prevent a blowout.

parts.name: Derrick / mast
parts.fn: Steel tower carrying the traveling block and drill string.

parts.name: Top drive & traveling block
parts.fn: Turn the drill pipe and raise or lower it.

parts.name: Drill pipe & bit
parts.fn: Carry rotation and mud to the bottom; the bit crushes the rock.

parts.name: Mud pump
parts.fn: Pushes drilling mud into the drill pipe.

parts.name: Mud tank & shaker
parts.fn: Hold the mud and screen out cuttings.

parts.name: Casing & cement
parts.fn: Steel wall of the hole, locked in place with cement.

parts.name: BOP
parts.fn: Safety valves that prevent a blowout.

parts.name: Reservoir
parts.fn: The oil-bearing rock being targeted.

stages.inp: drilling mud, casing, cement, bits, engine power
stages.out: a well ready for completion and production
civil: The well pad must be level, compacted and well drained to carry the rig and heavy equipment; it is often topped with compacted fill or temporary mats.
The cellar (pit under the rig) holds the wellhead and BOP; its walls need earth retention and drainage so it does not collapse or flood.
Mud pits or tanks need bunds and an impermeable liner so mud and drilling fluids do not contaminate the soil.
check: Mud weight and mud tank volume (signs of a kick or lost circulation).
Mud pump pressure and top drive torque.
Pressure tests of the BOP and casing before drilling continues.
stages.note: A rig is temporary: once the well is done it moves to the next location.

stages.name: Well with ESP
stages.fn: Lifts oil, water and gas from the reservoir to the surface with an electric submersible pump at the bottom of the well. Usually chosen for high-rate wells.
stages.story: After drilling and completion, the well needs help when reservoir pressure cannot push the fluid to the surface. In an ESP well a multistage pump and an electric motor are run on the end of the tubing, below the liquid level. Power from the surface (through the VSD) reaches the motor along a cable strapped to the tubing. The motor turns dozens of impellers; each stage adds pressure until the fluid is pushed up the tubing to the wellhead and into the flowline.
steps: Power from the transformer enters the VSD (variable speed drive), which sets the motor frequency and speed.
The downhole power cable carries the power to the motor at the bottom of the well.
The motor turns the shaft. The protector seals motor oil from well fluid; the intake draws fluid in and the gas separator releases free gas.
The staged impellers raise the pressure bit by bit so the fluid rises up the tubing.
At the wellhead (Christmas tree), valves control and secure the flow out to the flowline toward the manifold.
A downhole pressure and temperature sensor sends data to the VSD to adjust the pump speed.

parts.name: Wellhead
parts.fn: Control and safety valves at the top of the well (Christmas tree).

parts.name: VSD / panel
parts.fn: Sets motor speed and protects against overload.

parts.name: Power cable
parts.fn: Carries power from the surface to the motor downhole.

parts.name: Tubing
parts.fn: The pipe the fluid rises through.

parts.name: Casing
parts.fn: The steel wall of the well.

parts.name: Multistage pump
parts.fn: Impellers and diffusers that raise fluid pressure.

parts.name: Intake / gas separator
parts.fn: Draws fluid into the pump and separates free gas.

parts.name: Protector & motor
parts.fn: Electric motor turning the pump; the protector seals motor oil.

parts.name: Perforations
parts.fn: Holes in the casing where reservoir fluid enters the well.

stages.inp: power from the transformer via the VSD; reservoir fluid
stages.out: oil + water + gas through the flowline to the manifold
civil: The wellhead sits on a cellar or a small concrete foundation; the main loads are its own weight and the pull of the flowline.
The VSD and panel need a foundation or skid, a roof or enclosure, protection from water and room for cooling.
The power cable to the well needs a cable route (trench or poles) with mechanical protection.
check: Motor current (amps) and VSD frequency.
Pump intake pressure and the liquid level in the well.
Cable and motor insulation (megger) and vibration.
stages.note: This is a generic example. Other artificial lift methods: gas lift (pressurized gas lightens the fluid column), PCP, and hydraulic pumps. The choice depends on the well and its fluid; adjust to what is used in your field.

stages.name: Well with Pumpjack
stages.fn: The pumpjack strokes the sucker rods up and down so the pump at the bottom lifts the fluid; suited to shallow to medium wells with low to moderate rates.
stages.story: For wells with low to moderate rates, a simple way to lift fluid is the pumpjack. A surface motor turns the crank and counterweight; the pitman and walking beam turn that rotation into the up-and-down motion of the horsehead. The horsehead moves the polished rod and the sucker rod string, which stroke the plunger of the pump at the bottom of the well. Two valves inside the pump open and close in turn, so each stroke lifts a little fluid.
steps: The electric motor turns the gearbox; the crank and counterweight rotate (the counterweight balances the weight of the rods).
The pitman links the crank to the walking beam, which rocks like a seesaw.
The horsehead pulls the polished rod and sucker rods up (upstroke) and then lowers them (downstroke).
Upstroke: the traveling valve closes and the plunger lifts the fluid column above it; the standing valve opens and fresh fluid enters the barrel.
Downstroke: the standing valve closes and the traveling valve opens, so the plunger moves down through the fluid trapped in the barrel.
Fluid rises step by step up the tubing to the wellhead and the flowline.

parts.name: Motor & gearbox
parts.fn: Turn the crank through speed reduction.

parts.name: Crank & counterweight
parts.fn: Balance the rod weight and turn rotation into motion.

parts.name: Pitman & walking beam
parts.fn: Pass the crank motion on as a rocking beam.

parts.name: Horsehead
parts.fn: Beam end that pulls the polished rod straight.

parts.name: Polished rod
parts.fn: The rod that moves in and out of the wellhead through the stuffing box.

parts.name: Sucker rods
parts.fn: String of rods carrying the motion down to the pump.

parts.name: Barrel & plunger
parts.fn: Piston pump at the bottom that lifts the fluid.

parts.name: Traveling valve
parts.fn: Valve on the plunger: closed going up, open going down.

parts.name: Standing valve
parts.fn: Valve at the barrel bottom: open going up, closed going down.

stages.inp: power to the motor; reservoir fluid
stages.out: oil + water + gas through the flowline to the manifold
civil: A pumpjack puts cyclic loads (up-down motion and vibration) on its concrete foundation; the foundation is designed for dynamic loads and the overturning moment of the counterweight.
The foundation must be level and aligned with the wellhead so the polished rod runs straight and the stuffing box does not wear quickly.
Soft soil risks uneven settlement that tilts the unit; ground improvement or a wider foundation may be needed.
check: Dynamometer card (rod load against position) to judge pump condition.
Counterweight balance and gearbox condition.
Stuffing box leaks.
stages.note: Not the only method: high-rate light-oil wells usually use ESP or gas lift. The picture only shows that the lift method can differ from well to well.

stages.name: Manifold
stages.fn: Merges the flow from many wells and routes it to the production separator; one well can be switched to the test separator to test its output.
stages.story: One gathering station serves many wells. Each well's flow arrives through its own flowline at the manifold. Here valves decide where each well goes: most go into the production header toward the production separator, while one well at a time can be switched to the test header toward the test separator so its output (oil, water, gas) can be measured. After the test the well goes back to the production header and the next well takes its turn (well test).
steps: Each well's flowline reaches the manifold, each with an isolation valve.
A well that is not under test: its valve to the production header is open and its valve to the test header is closed.
A well to be tested: its production valve is closed and its test valve is open, so its flow goes to the test separator.
The test separator measures that well's oil, water and gas rates for a few hours.
When done, the valves are returned and the next well takes its turn.
A pressure gauge helps the operator confirm there is no blockage or leak.

parts.name: Well flowline
parts.fn: Pipe from each well to the manifold.

parts.name: Isolation valve
parts.fn: Opens or closes each well's route to a header.

parts.name: Production header
parts.fn: Collecting pipe toward the production separator.

parts.name: Test header
parts.fn: Collecting pipe only for the well under test.

parts.name: Pressure gauge
parts.fn: Monitors header pressure.

parts.name: To production separator
parts.fn: Combined flow of the producing wells.

parts.name: To test separator
parts.fn: Flow of the single well under test.

stages.inp: fluid from the flowlines of many wells
stages.out: the combined stream to the production separator, and one well to the test separator
civil: The manifold and piping rest on concrete sleepers or pipe supports; spacing and height are set so the pipe does not sag and thermal expansion is accommodated.
Sleeper foundations should be checked for settlement: uneven settlement overstresses the pipe joints.
The area has drainage and a concrete or gravel floor so spills are easy to clean up.
check: Header pressure and the pressure difference between wells.
Leaks at flanges and valves.
Well-test schedule and results for each well.

stages.name: Separator
stages.fn: Splits gas, oil and water by density. The production separator handles the combined stream; the test separator measures one well.
stages.story: Well fluid is a mix of oil, water and gas. In the separator the flow slows down so gravity splits the three: gas rises to the top space, oil floats in the middle and water settles at the bottom. Gas leaves from the top through a mist extractor that catches liquid droplets; oil spills over a weir into the oil compartment; water is drawn off the bottom. Level and pressure control valves keep the liquid levels and the pressure steady.
steps: Fluid enters through the inlet nozzle and hits the inlet diverter, so its speed drops and the phases begin to separate.
In the calm vessel, gas rises while water droplets sink through the oil because of the density difference.
The mist extractor near the gas outlet catches fine liquid droplets so the gas leaves dry.
Oil spills over the weir into the oil compartment and leaves through the oil outlet, controlled by a level valve (LCV).
Water collects at the bottom and leaves through the water outlet; the level glass and transmitter monitor the levels.
A pressure valve (PCV) on the gas line holds the separator pressure; gas goes to the compressor or the flare.

parts.name: Inlet & diverter
parts.fn: Slow the incoming flow and start the separation.

parts.name: Gas space
parts.fn: Where gas collects above the liquid.

parts.name: Mist extractor
parts.fn: Catches fine liquid droplets from the gas.

parts.name: Oil zone
parts.fn: The oil layer above the water.

parts.name: Water zone
parts.fn: Water settles below.

parts.name: Weir
parts.fn: Plate that sets the oil height and forms the oil compartment.

parts.name: Level glass & control
parts.fn: Monitor and control the liquid levels.

parts.name: Gas/oil/water outlets
parts.fn: Three exits, each with a control valve.

stages.inp: oil + water + gas from the manifold
stages.out: gas to the compressor/flare, oil to the wash tank, water to produced-water treatment
civil: A horizontal vessel rests on two saddles on a concrete foundation; the foundation carries the vessel full of water (hydrotest) plus wind and seismic loads.
One saddle is fixed and the other slides to allow thermal expansion; anchor bolts and base plates must match.
A curb (small dike) and drainage around the skid catch oil drips.
check: Oil-water interface level and total level.
Separator pressure and control valve openings.
Gas quality (liquid carry-over) and water cut of the outgoing oil.

stages.name: Gas Boot
stages.alias: Gas release vessel on top of the wash tank
stages.fn: An upright vessel on top of the wash tank that releases gas from the oil before the liquid goes down into the tank, so gas bubbles do not disturb the water settling.
stages.story: Oil leaving the separator still holds dissolved gas and a little free gas. As the pressure drops toward atmospheric, that gas comes out of solution (flashing) and forms bubbles; if these bubbles went into the wash tank they would stir the liquid and hinder the water from settling. So the fluid first enters the gas boot: its speed drops, the gas separates into the upper space and leaves through the vent to the gas line (or a vapour recovery system and flare), while the calm liquid goes down the downcomer into the wash tank. The liquid height in the boot also gives a head that helps push the fluid down to the spreader.
steps: Fluid from the separator enters the gas boot through the inlet on the side of the vessel.
An inlet diffuser (spreader plate) slows the flow so gas bubbles can separate from the liquid.
As the pressure drops toward atmospheric, dissolved gas leaves the oil (flashing) and rises into the gas space.
Gas leaves through the vent at the top, passes a flame arrestor, and goes to the gas line or a vapour recovery system.
Gas-free liquid collects at the bottom of the boot and goes down the downcomer.
The liquid level in the boot is kept in range: too low and gas follows the liquid into the tank, too high and liquid spills into the gas line.

parts.name: Inlet & diffuser
parts.fn: Admit the fluid and slow it down.

parts.name: Gas space
parts.fn: Where gas separates from the liquid.

parts.name: Vent & flame arrestor
parts.fn: Gas exit; the flame arrestor stops a flame from travelling back.

parts.name: Gas line
parts.fn: To the gas line, vapour recovery, or the flare.

parts.name: Liquid level
parts.fn: Liquid height in the boot that provides the head.

parts.name: Downcomer
parts.fn: Pipe guiding the liquid into the wash tank.

parts.name: Wash tank
parts.fn: Where the liquid is washed and the water settles (see number 7).

parts.name: Pressure & level gauge
parts.fn: Monitor the pressure and liquid level in the boot.

stages.inp: oil + water + dissolved gas from the separator
stages.out: gas to the gas line; gas-free liquid to the wash tank through the downcomer
civil: A slender, tall gas boot on the tank roof is checked for wind load, and its seat on the roof or tank frame (or its own support structure) must be strong enough.
The weight of the boot, its liquid and the piping adds load on the tank roof; the roof plate and joints are checked locally and must not upset the tank roof design.
The vent and gas line need adequate pipe supports; the area around the vent is classified as hazardous, so electrical equipment nearby must be suitable.
check: Pressure in the boot, and the condition of the vent and flame arrestor (not blocked).
Liquid level in the boot (never spilling into the gas line).
Gas leaks at flanges and joints.
stages.note: At some facilities the gas boot is a separate vessel beside the tank, or another vessel does its job; in the picture the boot sits on top of the wash tank.

stages.name: Wash Tank
stages.fn: Dehydration: lets the water still carried by the oil settle out, helped by demulsifier chemicals when needed, until the water cut (BS&W) is within limits.
stages.story: Oil from the separator still carries fine water that will not simply sink because it is an emulsion. In the wash tank (gun barrel) the oil enters through a downcomer to the lower part of the tank and leaves through a spreader inside the water layer. As it rises through the water (water wash), small water droplets coalesce and settle; demulsifier helps break the emulsion. Clean oil collects on top and spills to the outlet; water is drawn off through the water leg, which sets the oil-water interface.
steps: Wet oil enters through the gas boot, where carried gas is released and sent to the gas line.
The downcomer guides the liquid down and the spreader distributes it evenly inside the water layer.
Demulsifier is injected into the inlet line to break the emulsion film.
Oil rises through the water (water wash) while water droplets merge and settle.
Clean oil builds up on top and spills over to the oil outlet toward the storage tank.
Water leaves through the water leg; its height sets the oil-water interface inside the tank.

parts.name: Gas boot
parts.fn: Releases gas from the incoming fluid (see number 6).

parts.name: Downcomer
parts.fn: Pipe guiding fluid to the lower part of the tank.

parts.name: Spreader
parts.fn: Perforated pipe that distributes fluid in the water layer.

parts.name: Water zone
parts.fn: The water layer where the oil is washed.

parts.name: Oil zone
parts.fn: Clean oil collecting on top.

parts.name: Oil outlet
parts.fn: Overflow and exit pipe for the oil.

parts.name: Water leg
parts.fn: External pipe that sets the interface and removes water.

parts.name: Demulsifier injection
parts.fn: Chemical that breaks the emulsion.

stages.out: clean oil to the storage tank, water to produced-water treatment
civil: A large-diameter atmospheric tank stands on a ring-wall foundation and a sand or gravel pad; uneven settlement can damage the tank bottom.
Full load (hydrotest) and wind load on the tall shell are checked for overturning and anchorage.
A dike or bund around the tank is sized to hold the specified volume if the tank leaks.
check: Oil-water interface height and temperature.
Water cut (BS&W) of the outgoing oil.
Demulsifier dosage.

stages.name: Storage Tank & Shipping Pump
stages.fn: Holds the oil once it meets specification, measures it, then pumps it through the export pipeline to its destination.
stages.story: Clean oil is gathered in the storage tank as a buffer: the flow from the wash tank can rise and fall while shipping is kept steady. From the tank the shipping pump raises the pressure; the oil passes a metering unit (meter, sometimes a LACT) so its volume is counted and a sample is taken, and then enters the export pipeline.
steps: Oil enters the tank through the inlet; the level rises and is read by the level gauge (ATG).
The vent or pressure-vacuum valve on the roof balances the vapour pressure as the level rises or falls.
When the level is sufficient the shipping pump starts; oil leaves near the bottom of the tank to the pump suction.
The impeller raises the oil pressure; the electric motor turns the shaft.
The oil passes a meter (and sampler) so volume and quality are recorded.
Valves and a check valve control the flow and prevent backflow, then the oil enters the export pipeline.

parts.name: Fixed-roof tank
parts.fn: Holds the clean oil.

parts.name: Level gauge (ATG)
parts.fn: Measures the oil height in the tank.

parts.name: Vent / PV valve
parts.fn: Balances vapour pressure above the oil.

parts.name: Inlet
parts.fn: Oil arrives from the wash tank.

parts.name: Shipping pump & motor
parts.fn: Raise the oil pressure for shipping.

parts.name: Meter
parts.fn: Measures the volume of oil shipped.

parts.name: Valve & check valve
parts.fn: Control the flow and prevent backflow.

parts.name: Export pipeline
parts.fn: The oil shipping route.

parts.name: Bund (dike)
parts.fn: Holds the oil if the tank leaks.

stages.out: pressurized oil into the export pipeline
civil: Tank foundation: a concrete ring wall or a pad with ground improvement; designed for bearing capacity, settlement and overturning from wind or earthquake (see Calculations → Tank & Equipment Foundations).
Pumps and motors sit on skids or concrete foundations with anchor bolts; rotating-machine foundations account for vibration.
The bund holds a specified minimum volume, has an impermeable floor, and drains to an oil catcher.
check: Tank level and temperature, and any water at the bottom.
Pump pressure and current, and vibration.
Meter accuracy (calibration or proving).
stages.note: Destination and facility order differ from field to field; this is a general picture.

stages.name: Compressor & Flare
stages.fn: Gas from the separator is compressed so it can be used; gas that cannot be used, or must be released in an emergency, is burned in a controlled way at the flare.
stages.story: Alongside the oil, the separator produces gas. The gas passes a scrubber to remove liquid, then the compressor raises its pressure so it can be used: as fuel in the facility, for gas lift, or to be sent to a user. In a reciprocating compressor the piston moves back and forth: moving back, the suction valve opens and gas enters; moving forward, the suction valve closes, the gas is squeezed, and then the discharge valve opens. Gas that cannot be used, or that must be released on over-pressure or in an emergency, goes to the flare and is burned in a controlled way.
steps: Gas from the separator enters the suction scrubber; carried liquid settles out and is drained.
Suction stroke: the piston moves away from the cylinder head, pressure drops, the suction valve opens and gas enters.
Compression stroke: the piston moves back toward the head, the suction valve closes, and the gas pressure rises.
When the pressure exceeds the discharge line pressure, the discharge valve opens and pressurized gas leaves.
The gas is cooled in the cooler and goes on to use (fuel, gas lift, or export).
Excess gas or emergency relief flows to the knock-out drum and then the flare, where the pilot ignites and burns it.

parts.name: Suction scrubber
parts.fn: Removes liquid from the incoming gas.

parts.name: Cylinder & piston
parts.fn: Compress the gas with a back-and-forth stroke.

parts.name: Suction valve
parts.fn: Opens during the suction stroke.

parts.name: Discharge valve
parts.fn: Opens once the gas is pressurized enough.

parts.name: Crank, rod & flywheel
parts.fn: Turn rotation into piston motion and smooth the speed.

parts.name: Cooler
parts.fn: Cools the gas after compression.

parts.name: Knock-out drum
parts.fn: Holds liquid from relief gas before the flare.

parts.name: Flare & pilot
parts.fn: Burn the relief gas safely.

stages.out: pressurized gas for fuel/process/gas lift; the rest goes to the flare
civil: A reciprocating compressor produces repeating unbalanced forces: its foundation is usually a massive concrete block separate from the surrounding floor, with a vibration check (natural frequency kept away from the operating frequency) and strong anchor bolts.
A tall flare stack carries wind and earthquake loads: its foundation is checked for overturning, and safe distance from heat radiation is set in the layout.
Gas piping vibrates: supports and spacing are designed to prevent fatigue of the joints.
check: Suction and discharge pressure at each stage, and discharge temperature.
Vibration and unusual noise.
Flare pilot flame and the liquid level in the knock-out drum.

stages.name: Water Injection Pump
stages.fn: Treated produced water is pressurized and injected back into the reservoir through an injection well (waterflood).
stages.story: Water produced along with the oil is not simply dumped. After it is separated and treated (filtered and stripped of residual oil), the high-pressure injection pump pushes it back into the reservoir through an injection well. The water keeps the reservoir pressure up and pushes oil toward the surrounding producing wells (waterflood), so production lasts longer and produced water is managed.
steps: Produced water from the separator and wash tank is collected in the water tank and treated (filtered and de-oiled).
The injection pump raises the water pressure above the reservoir pressure.
The pressurized water flows through the injection line to the injection wellhead.
Water goes down the injection well tubing and leaves into the reservoir through the perforations.
The water front sweeps through the rock and pushes oil toward the producing wells.
Reservoir pressure is maintained, so the producing wells keep flowing.

stages.inp: produced water from the separator and wash tank
stages.out: high-pressure water to the injection well
civil: A high-pressure pump vibrates: its foundation or skid and anchor bolts are designed for dynamic loads.
High-pressure injection lines need strong pipe supports, and thrust blocks at bends when the pipe is buried.
The water tank and pump area need bunds and drainage so saline water and residual oil do not contaminate the soil.
check: Injection rate and pressure of each well.
Water quality (solids, residual oil, corrosion).
Response of the producing wells (production gain or water breakthrough).

stages.name: Power Pole
stages.fn: Holds medium-voltage conductors overhead to carry power from the source to the wells and production facilities.
stages.story: All the pumps, motors, compressors and VSDs above need electricity. Medium-voltage power from the source (grid or power plant) travels along an overhead line on poles. Three conductors (three phases) are fixed to insulators on the cross-arm so they never touch the pole. Along the route there are protections: arresters send lightning strikes to the ground, fuse cut-outs open a branch on over-current, and grounding carries fault current into the earth. At the facility the line branches to the transformer.
steps: The three-phase conductors carry power from the source; the voltage of each phase swings in turn, 120° apart.
Insulators on the cross-arm hold the conductors and keep their voltage away from the pole.
The wire is left hanging (sag) between poles so it is safe from tension as temperature changes and wind blows.
The arrester sends voltage surges from lightning to the ground.
The fuse cut-out opens a branch on over-current or a fault.
A ground wire along the pole carries fault current to a ground rod in the soil.

parts.name: Insulator
parts.fn: Separates the live wire from the pole.

parts.name: Cross-arm
parts.fn: Arm holding the insulators and wires.

parts.name: 3-phase conductors
parts.fn: Three wires carrying the power.

parts.name: Arrester
parts.fn: Sends lightning strikes to the ground.

parts.name: Fuse cut-out

parts.name: Pole

parts.name: Pole foundation
parts.fn: Embedded part that resists overturning and uplift.

parts.name: Grounding
parts.fn: Wire and rod connecting to the earth.

stages.inp: power from the grid or a power plant
civil: A pole takes lateral load from wind and wire tension plus a moment at its base; the embedment or foundation (spread or bored) is checked for overturning and uplift.
Angle poles and dead-end poles take one-sided tension, so they get guy wires or a larger foundation.
Soft or waterlogged soil reduces lateral resistance; poles near roads need protection from vehicle impact.
check: Pole lean and foundation condition (erosion, cracks).
Condition of insulators, arresters and connections.
Clearance of the wires from ground, equipment and pipes.
stages.note: Power source and voltage differ from field to field; this is only a general picture.

stages.name: Transformer
stages.fn: Steps the medium voltage of the distribution line down to the low voltage used by pump motors, the compressor, ESP VSDs, lighting and instruments.
stages.story: The distribution line carries a medium voltage that is too high for the motors and panels in the facility. The transformer steps it down to low voltage. The principle: alternating current in the primary winding creates a changing magnetic field in the iron core; that field passes through the secondary winding and induces a voltage there. Because the secondary has fewer turns, its voltage is lower. The core, windings and transformer oil (insulation and cooling) sit inside a finned tank; heat leaves through the radiator.
steps: Medium voltage enters through the HV bushing to the primary winding (many turns).
Alternating current in the primary creates a changing magnetic flux in the iron core.
The flux circulates around the core and passes through the secondary winding.
In the secondary (fewer turns) a low voltage is induced; the turns ratio sets the voltage ratio.
Losses become heat; the transformer oil circulates (convection) and carries the heat to the radiator fins.
Low voltage leaves through the LV bushing to cables toward motors, VSDs and panels; fuses and arresters protect the transformer.

parts.name: HV bushing
parts.fn: Insulated pass-through where the medium-voltage wire enters.

parts.name: Primary winding
parts.fn: Many turns that receive the incoming voltage.

parts.name: Iron core
parts.fn: Path of the magnetic flux from primary to secondary.

parts.name: Secondary winding
parts.fn: Fewer turns that produce the low voltage.

parts.name: LV bushing
parts.fn: Where the low voltage leaves.

parts.name: Transformer oil
parts.fn: Insulation and coolant.

parts.name: Radiator
parts.fn: Fins that shed the oil's heat.

parts.name: Tank
parts.fn: Container for core, windings and oil.

stages.inp: medium voltage from the power pole
stages.out: low voltage through cables (underground in the picture) to motors and panels
civil: An oil-filled transformer is heavy: it stands on a concrete pad designed for its total weight and, where needed, wind or seismic loads.
Around the pad there is a bund or pit (oil containment) sized to the transformer oil volume, so spills do not contaminate the soil.
Safe distances between transformers and to buildings or tanks are set in the layout; fire walls are used where distance is not enough.
check: Oil temperature and level.
Load (current) against capacity and phase balance.
Oil leaks, abnormal noise, and bushing condition.
